knowledge:
- key_parameters: features=In analyzeFeatures(), a TxFeatures object used to guide the analysis based on existing annotation ;; which=In analyzeFeatures() or predictTxFeatures(), a GRanges object specifying the genomic region of interest for de novo prediction ;; min_denominator=In analyzeVariants() or getSGVariantCounts(), the minimum compatible fragment count required at either the start or end of a variant to avoid setting relative usage estimates to NA ;; cores=Integer specifying the number of cores for parallel processing ;; max_complexity=In prediction functions, controls skipping of regions with high split-read complexity to prevent memory issues ;; min_overhang=In predictTxFeatures(), set to NULL when running on individual samples to suppress terminal exon processing before merging
- alternatives: DEXSeq=For performing statistical testing of differential exon/variant usage ;; limma (diffSplice with voom)=For performing statistical testing of differential splice variant usage using single counts per variant
- when_to_use: When analyzing alternative splicing events from RNA-seq data mapped to a reference genome in BAM format, either using existing transcript annotations or predicting novel splice features de novo, and wishing to quantify local splice variant usage (PSI) and visualize splice graphs.
- pitfalls: BAM files must be indexed and generated with a splice-aware aligner (e.g., GSNAP, HISAT, STAR) that outputs the custom 'XS' tag for spliced reads ;; lib_size must reflect the total number of aligned fragments in the original BAM files (even if subsetted) for accurate FPKM calculation ;; variant effect prediction (predictVariantEffects) is relatively slow and should only be run on select variants ;; high split-read complexity regions can cause memory issues, which can be resolved by adjusting max_complexity or excluding problematic regions like mitochondrial genes

workflows.name: annotation_guided_splice_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze and quantify splice features and variants using existing transcript annotations.
input: file_bam (Indexed BAM files from splice-aware aligner)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert TxDb annotation to transcript features using convertToTxFeatures() ;; 2. Convert transcript features to splice graph features and count compatible fragments using analyzeFeatures() ;; 3. Plot splice graph and feature expression using plotFeatures()
workflows.code:
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)
library(GenomeInfoDb)  # for keepSeqlevels() and seqlevelsStyle()
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
txdb <- keepSeqlevels(txdb, "chr16")
seqlevelsStyle(txdb) <- "NCBI"
txf_ucsc <- convertToTxFeatures(txdb)
txf_ucsc <- txf_ucsc[txf_ucsc %over% gr]
sgfc_ucsc <- analyzeFeatures(si, features = txf_ucsc)
df <- plotFeatures(sgfc_ucsc, geneID = 1)

workflows.name: de_novo_splice_analysis
workflows.intent: Predict novel splice features de novo from RNA-seq data, annotate them, identify splice variants, and predict their functional effects.
input: file_bam (Indexed BAM files from splice-aware aligner)
gr (GRanges object of genomic region of interest)
txdb (TxDb annotation object for annotating predicted features)
Hsapiens (BSgenome object for variant effect prediction)
workflows.stages: 1. Predict transcript features and count compatible fragments using analyzeFeatures() ;; 2. Annotate predicted features with known transcripts using annotate() ;; 3. Identify splice variants and estimate relative usage using analyzeVariants() ;; 4. Predict variant effects on protein-coding potential using predictVariantEffects() ;; 5. Obtain single counts per variant for differential testing using getSGVariantCounts()
workflows.code:
sgfc_pred <- analyzeFeatures(si, which = gr)
sgfc_pred <- annotate(sgfc_pred, txf_ucsc)
df <- plotFeatures(sgfc_pred, geneID = 1, color_novel = "red")
sgvc_pred <- analyzeVariants(sgfc_pred)
plotVariants(sgvc_pred, eventID = 1, color_novel = "red")
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)
seqlevelsStyle(Hsapiens) <- "NCBI"
vep <- predictVariantEffects(sgv_pred, txdb, Hsapiens)
sgv <- rowRanges(sgvc_pred)
sgvc <- getSGVariantCounts(sgv, sample_info = si)
x <- counts(sgvc)
vid <- variantID(sgvc)
eid <- eventID(sgvc)

workflows.name: step_by_step_splice_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform de novo splice feature prediction, quantification, and variant identification using individual step-by-step functions for advanced control.
input: file_bam (Indexed BAM files from splice-aware aligner)
gr (GRanges object of genomic region of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Predict transcript features using predictTxFeatures() ;; 2. Convert predicted transcript features to splice graph features using convertToSGFeatures() ;; 3. Annotate splice graph features using annotate() ;; 4. Get compatible fragment counts for splice graph features using getSGFeatureCounts() ;; 5. Find splice variants from splice graph features using findSGVariants() ;; 6. Get variant counts and relative frequencies using getSGVariantCounts()
workflows.code:
txf <- predictTxFeatures(si, gr)
sgf <- convertToSGFeatures(txf)
sgf <- annotate(sgf, txf_ucsc)
sgfc <- getSGFeatureCounts(si, sgf)
sgv <- findSGVariants(sgf)
sgvc <- getSGVariantCounts(sgv, sgfc)
